title: Model quality starts from data pipeline
text:
Model quality starts from data pipeline
Reality
• Same architecture ̸= same performance.
• Data split, augmentation, preprocessing, and batching directly affect
what the model learns.
• Many training bugs are caused by data pipeline errors, not model
architecture errors.
Takeaway
Model system = Architecture + Data Pipeline + Optimization.

title: Train / Validation / Test split
text:
Train / Validation / Test split
Roles
• Train set: learn model parameters.
• Validation set: tune hyperparameters and select checkpoints.
• Test set: final evaluation only.
Critical rule
Never use the test set during training, tuning, checkpoint selection, or early
stopping.

title: Data leakage: very common and very dangerous
text:
Data leakage: very common and very dangerous
Typical examples
• Same video frames, near-duplicate frames, or adjacent frames appear in
both train and test.
• Same patient, same subject, same camera scene, or same object instance
appears across splits.
• Augmented copies are generated first, then split later.
Takeaway
Leakage ⇒fake high accuracy because the model sees overly similar samples
during training.

title: From distribution mismatch to augmentation
text:
From distribution mismatch to augmentation
Why augmentation is needed
• Real-world images vary in viewpoint, lighting, scale, background, blur,
and occlusion.
• Training datasets are usually limited and biased.
• Augmentation simulates plausible real-world variations.
Takeaway
Augmentation is not just “more data”; it is a way to shape the training
distribution.

title: Label quality matters
text:
Label quality matters
Reality
• Labels may be noisy, inconsistent, incomplete, or ambiguous.
• Different annotators may label the same image differently.
• Wrong labels introduce wrong learning signals.
Impact
Bad labels reduce the upper bound of model performance, even with a strong
architecture.
Takeaway
Garbage in ⇒garbage out.

title: Label representation
text:
Label representation
Common tasks
• Classification: integer label.
• Multi-label classification: multi-hot vector.
• Segmentation: mask of shape (H, W ) or (C, H, W ).
• Detection: boxes + class labels.
Takeaway
Data format must match model output, loss function, and evaluation metric.

title: Augmentation categories
text:
Augmentation categories
Common types
• Geometric: crop, flip, rotate, scale, perspective.
• Photometric: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, blur.
• Regularization: MixUp, CutMix, Random Erasing.
Important constraint
Augmentation must preserve the semantic label.
Takeaway
Good augmentation improves generalization; bad augmentation changes the
task.

title: Train vs evaluation transforms
text:
Train vs evaluation transforms
Training
• Use random augmentation.
• Goal: expose the model to many plausible variants.
Validation / Test
• Use deterministic preprocessing.
• Goal: obtain stable and comparable metrics.
Common mistake
Using random augmentation in validation makes metrics noisy and unfair.

title: Augmentation for structured targets
text:
Augmentation for structured targets
Classification
Image-only augmentation is often enough if the label is unchanged.
Detection / Segmentation
Geometric augmentation must also transform:
• bounding boxes,
• masks,
• keypoints,
• polygons.
Takeaway
For structured prediction, image and annotation transforms must be
synchronized.

title: Pipeline affects optimization
text:
Pipeline affects optimization
Why the optimizer feels the pipeline
• Augmentation changes the input distribution.
• Sampling changes the class distribution inside minibatches.
• Batch composition affects BatchNorm statistics.
• Collate and resizing policies affect tensor shapes and memory usage.
Takeaway
Data pipeline directly influences optimization dynamics.

title: Collate function
text:
Collate function
Role
• Convert a list of samples into one batch.
• Default collate stacks tensors with identical shapes.
Need custom collate when
• images have different sizes,
• targets have variable lengths,
• detection boxes or segmentation masks need special handling.
Takeaway
Dataset returns one sample; collate builds a batch.

title: Collate example: simple classification
text:
Collate example: simple classification
import
torch
def
collate_fn(batch):
xs , ys = zip(* batch)
xs = torch.stack(xs , dim =0)
ys = torch.tensor(ys)
return xs , ys
Requirement
All images must already have the same tensor shape.

title: DataLoader parameters
text:
DataLoader parameters
Main parameters
• batch size: number of samples per batch.
• shuffle: randomize sample order during training.
• num workers: number of parallel loading processes.
• pin memory: speed up CPU-to-GPU transfer.
• collate fn: custom batch construction.
Takeaway
DataLoader controls both statistical behavior and hardware throughput.

title: Pipeline bottleneck: diagnosis and actions
text:
Pipeline bottleneck: diagnosis and actions
Symptoms
• GPU utilization is low while CPU has spare capacity.
• Training loop spends large time waiting for the next batch.
• Increasing model size does not reduce throughput much.
Actions
• Increase num workers gradually and measure samples/sec.
• Enable pin memory=True for faster host-to-device transfer.
• Use persistent workers=True to reduce worker restart overhead.
• Cache or accelerate heavy decode and augmentation operations.
Goal
Keep GPU busy without exhausting RAM, CPU, or disk bandwidth.

title: Class imbalance: why it hurts
text:
Class imbalance: why it hurts
Problem
• Rare classes are sampled less often.
• Gradients are dominated by frequent classes.
• Overall accuracy may look good while minority-class recall is poor.
Common solutions
• Sampling-level: weighted or class-balanced sampler.
• Loss-level: class-weighted cross-entropy or focal loss.
• Evaluation-level: per-class precision, recall, and F1.

title: Imbalance code: weighted sampler + weighted loss
text:
Imbalance code: weighted sampler + weighted loss
import
torch
from
torch.utils.data
import
WeightedRandomSampler
labels = torch.tensor(train_labels)
# shape [N]
class_count = torch.bincount(labels)
class_w = 1.0 / class_count.float ().clamp(min =1)
sample_w = class_w[labels]
sampler = WeightedRandomSampler (
weights=sample_w ,
num_samples=len(sample_w),
replacement=True
)
criterion = torch.nn. CrossEntropyLoss (
weight=class_w.to(device)
)

title: Reproducibility code snippet

Reproducibility code snippet
import
random
import
numpy as np
import
torch
seed = 42
random.seed(seed)
np.random.seed(seed)
torch.manual_seed(seed)
torch.cuda. manual_seed_all (seed)
def
seed_worker(worker_id):
worker_seed = seed + worker_id
random.seed(worker_seed)
np.random.seed(worker_seed)
g = torch.Generator ()
g.manual_seed(seed)

title: Debug checklist
text:
Debug checklist
Before training
• Visualize a batch after all transforms.
• Check tensor shape: (B, C, H, W ).
• Check tensor range before and after normalization.
• Check label alignment.
During training
• Check loss decreases on a small subset.
• Overfit a tiny dataset to detect pipeline/model bugs.
• Monitor GPU utilization and loading time.
Takeaway
Debug the pipeline before blaming the architecture.
